page: The Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a memory-optimized server configuration within the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It is built on dedicated AMD EPYC x86_64 processors, delivering 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs running at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes hardware vector and cryptographic instruction sets, such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16 extensions, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance is provisioned with 384 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB RAM-to-vCPU allocation ratio. Local persistence is provided by an integrated 2,880 GB NVMe solid-state drive, accompanied by one complimentary public IPv4 address without hardware GPU acceleration.

Benchmark evaluations position this instance in the upper tiers for both memory subsystem throughput and multi-threaded computation. In uncached large-block tests, memory bandwidth achieves 414.9 GB/sec read and 213.09 GB/sec write speeds, placing it in the top 10 percent of evaluated systems. Compute benchmarking corroborates this throughput, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,345.0, a Clang compilation score of 58,474.0, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 88,688.86. In application-level benchmarks, the configuration demonstrates 85.37 million Redis SET operations per second and 44.4 GB/sec of static web serving throughput.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the machine provides substantial resource density by coupling a dedicated 48-vCPU slice with large memory arrays and fast local NVMe storage. Because the instance relies on central CPU execution without discrete GPU acceleration, throughput drops in large 70B parameter LLM inference tasks. Consequently, the instance delivers optimal operational efficiency when deployed for memory-dense enterprise workloads, including in-memory datastores, distributed caching clusters, large relational databases, code compilation pipelines, and transactional ETL data processing.
description: The Vultr vx1-m-48c-384g-2880s is a high-density, memory-optimized cloud server built on the AMD EPYC architecture. It delivers 48 dedicated vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 2.0 GHz, coupled with 384 GB of system memory and 2,880 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD storage. The x86_64 platform incorporates instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA-NI. Benchmarks reflect upper-tier performance, characterized by 414.9 GB/sec uncached read memory bandwidth, a Geekbench multi-core score of 26,345.0, and 85.37 million Redis SET operations per second. While lacking hardware GPU accelerators for large-model deep learning tasks, the dense 8 GB per vCPU memory profile and high NVMe capacity make this system highly cost-efficient for heavy in-memory datastores, massive Redis deployments, relational databases, software build farms, and high-throughput data processing pipelines.
